s.t: The Five Stairsteps' ‘O-o-h Child’ began as the B-side to their ‘Dear Prudence’ cover, but it broke out in Philadelphia and Detroit and reached number 8.
s.q: "O-o-h Child" as B-side. However, "O-o-h Child" broke out in the key markets of Philadelphia and Detroit to rise as high as #8 on the Billboard Hot 100

s.t: Curtis Mayfield's workload stopped him continuing to work with The Five Stairsteps, so Buddah Records reassigned them to Stan Vincent, who wrote ‘O-o-h Child’.
s.q: When Mayfield's workload precluded his continuing to work with the group, they were reassigned to Stan Vincent, an in-house producer for Buddah Records

s.t: The Five Stairsteps' ‘O-o-h Child’ has inspired more than twenty covers, including Dino's 1993 version, which reached number 27 on the Billboard Hot 100.
s.q: has inspired more than twenty covers since its release. ... cover of "O-o-h Child" reached No. 27 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1993.

s.t: Billboard ranked The Five Stairsteps' ‘O-o-h Child’ the 21st song of 1970, and Rolling Stone placed it at number 402 on its 500 Greatest Songs of All Time.
s.q: The song is ranked #402 on the Rolling Stone magazine's list of The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time. Billboard ranked the record as the No. 21 song of 1970.

f.t: Their name came from their mother, Betty Burke, who thought her children looked like stair steps when lined up by age.
f.q: named by Mrs. Burke who thought her children looked like stair steps when lined up according to their age

f.t: Their father, Clarence Burke Sr., was a Chicago police detective who also played bass behind them, managed them and co-wrote songs with Clarence Burke Jr. and Gregory Fowler.
f.q: Clarence Sr. was a detective for the Chicago Police Department. He backed the group on bass guitar, managed them, and co-wrote songs with Clarence Jr. and Gregory Fowler.

f.t: They were dubbed the ‘First Family of Soul’ because of a successful five-year chart run; the nickname was later passed on to the Jackson 5.
f.q: The Chicago group was dubbed "First Family of Soul" because of their successful five-year chart run; the moniker was later passed on to the Jackson 5.

f.t: As The Invisible Man's Band, they released a heavily disco-styled hit, ‘All Night Thing’, on a 1980 album; it returned the Burke brothers to the R&B top ten.
f.q: featured the heavily disco-styled hit "All Night Thing", which returned the Burke brothers to the top ten on the R&B chart.
